declarations.coverage: Intentionally empty content scope: factory workflow rules govern the whole repository and tracker work; factory configuration is a separate exact declaration.

Intentionally empty content scope: this declaration changes remote GitHub settings only through its canonical-labels and pull-request-integration fixes, and its checks read the optional repository-owned .github/pull-request-reviewer.json and .github/factory-review-policy.json without writing them. The repository-local origin identifies one github.com repository, lutzseverino/repo-canon (public), and the authenticated gh account has admin access, so remote configuration is authorized for this owner-requested update.

There are no concrete Project README targets. Repo Canon is one standards source at the repository root, whose root README is separately governed. The factory runtime moved to Scriptorium; test fixtures, vendor inputs and source operation directories are not maintained independent Projects.

Drafted from manifests and workspace configuration by `discovery/draft-typescript-node-stack-scope.mjs`: one `package.json` per Project, included when it matches the stack's manifest facts and excluded naming its differences otherwise. A maintained workspace root package is a Project alongside its members; a shared-only root is not. Uncertain root membership stays unresolved. A root package without workspace members is a Project.

candidates.reason: The root package is the repository's one Project (no workspace members, no pnpm-workspace.yaml) with its own development commands and kept sources. It matches the manifest facts (packageManager pnpm@11.28.8, pnpm-lock.yaml, engines.node >=24 <25 || >=26 <27, oxlint 1.86.0, Prettier 3.9.9, a validate script), and nothing contradicts the rest of the rules: tsconfig.json type-checks the JavaScript with TypeScript 7.0.2 checkJs, tests run with node --test, CI runs pnpm validate on Node.js 24 and 26 behind the required Test aggregate, the development guide's Setup and validation section names the tools, and no other stack applies.
